back: A long-term decline in the ability of land to support plants, animals and people.
Sheet: thin even layer removed. Rill: small channels that can be ploughed over. Gully: deep steep-sided channels that cannot.
Build-up of eroded soil on the beds of rivers, dams and wetlands; reduces dam capacity and makes rivers flood more easily.
Degradation of dry land until it becomes desert-like, caused by drought together with overgrazing, over-cultivation and deforestation.
Overgrazing, over-cultivation, ploughing up and down slopes, deforestation, veld fires, sand abstraction, gold panning, draining wetlands.
Contour ridges and ploughing, terracing, afforestation, conservation agriculture, controlled grazing, fireguards, check dams, stone lines.
Cheap, uses local materials and labour, supported by the community, and lasts after outside funding ends.
Zimbabwe's conservation agriculture programme: planting basins, minimum tillage, mulching and crop rotation.
African Union initiative launched in 2007 to restore degraded land in a belt across the Sahel.
